pamphlet_excerpts: Different American Indian cultural areas: Pueblos were made of different types of materials (p. 7).
Different American Indian cultural areas Principle 2: The Hopi and the Zuñi used stones that were mortared together and surfaced with plaster (p. 7).
Different American Indian cultural areas Principle 3: Rio Grande Indians constructed their homes from adobe bricks of sun-dried earth mixed with straw (p. 7).
Different American Indian cultural areas Principle 4: They stretched log beams across the roofs and covered them with poles, brush, and plaster (p. 7).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Different American Indian cultural areas): Sometimes the beams projected beyond the walls and were used as pegs to hang food for drying (p. 7).
Step 2 (Different American Indian cultural areas): The women owned the apartments and all of the furnishings (p. 7).
Step 3 (Different American Indian cultural areas): In the central plaza of the village, the people dug kivas, underground chambers where men conducted sacred rituals (p. 7).
Step 4 (Different American Indian cultural areas): Men also used the kivas as clubhouses, and women usually were not allowed to enter (p. 7).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: Why did American Indian nations across regions such as the Pacific Northwest, the Great Plains, and the Desert Southwest develop markedly different housing, diets, and clothing prior to European contact?
quiz_item.question: Why did American Indian nations across regions such as the Pacific Northwest, the Great Plains, and the Desert Southwest develop markedly different housing, diets, and clothing prior to European contact?
options: A. All tribes followed a single continental council that assigned different crafts and housing styles to each region by lottery.
B. Each Indigenous nation adapted its technology, shelter, foodways, and social organization to the specific geography, climate, and natural resources of its homeland.
C. Tribes in every region relied exclusively on imported European iron tools and domesticated horses for thousands of years before 1492.
D. Differences in shelter and diet were caused solely by proximity to Spanish missions established along the Atlantic seaboard.
choices: A. All tribes followed a single continental council that assigned different crafts and housing styles to each region by lottery.
B. Each Indigenous nation adapted its technology, shelter, foodways, and social organization to the specific geography, climate, and natural resources of its homeland.
C. Tribes in every region relied exclusively on imported European iron tools and domesticated horses for thousands of years before 1492.
D. Differences in shelter and diet were caused solely by proximity to Spanish missions established along the Atlantic seaboard.
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Each Indigenous nation adapted its technology, shelter, foodways, and social organization to the specific geography, climate, and natural resources of its homeland.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): American Indian cultures developed distinct lifeways (such as cedar plank houses in the Pacific Northwest, bison hide tipis on the Plains, and adobe pueblos in the Southwest) adapted directly to local ecosystems and resources.

pamphlet_excerpts: American Indian Tribe: An American Indian tribe, group: Using dugout canoes, Plateau tribes traveled and traded widely along the Columbia and Fraser river systems (p. 57).
American Indian Tribe Principle 2: An American Indian tribe, group Principle 2: From the west came sea otter pelts and ornamental shells (p. 57).
American Indian Tribe Principle 3: An American Indian tribe, group Principle 3: Deer skins, hemp for basket making, and bitter root were brought from the interior (p. 57).

American Indian Tribe Principle 4: An American Indian tribe, group Principle 4: All sorts of goods changed hands: dried salmon, candle fish oil, baskets, carvings, even the canoes in which the traders carried their wares (p. 57).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (American Indian Tribe): Step 1 (An American Indian tribe, group): When horses came to the Plateau in the early 18th c entury, tribes like the Yakima, Nez Perce, and Cayusebecame expert horse raise rs and traders (p. 57).
Step 2 (American Indian Tribe): Step 2 (An American Indian tribe, group): The Plateau Indians had a complex system of beliefs and ceremonies (p. 57).

Step 3 (American Indian Tribe): Step 3 (An American Indian tribe, group): Everyone sought visits from guardian spirits, and when someone felt they were about to be healed by their guardian spirit, there was a ceremony (p. 57).
Step 4 (American Indian Tribe): Step 4 (An American Indian tribe, group): Shamans had visions and appeared to the people in the guise of grizzly bears (p. 57).

pamphlet_excerpts: Learn Common Terms in An: Learn 10 Common Terms: Indians are relearning lost traditions and languages and reviving their arts and crafts, their songs, dances, and stories (p. 17).

Learn Common Terms in An Principle 2: Learn 10 Common Terms Principle 2: Many have chosen not to disappear into America's "melting pot." Indians are reclaiming control over what happens to them (p. 17).
Learn Common Terms in An Principle 3: Learn 10 Common Terms Principle 3: They want to decide for themselves how they will live in the modern world (p. 17).

Learn Common Terms in An Principle 4: Learn 10 Common Terms Principle 4: The question is, how can they keep cultural roots alive and protect and preserve tribal identities, yet still be a part of modern society (p. 17).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Learn Common Terms in An): Step 1 (Learn 10 Common Terms): There is no easy answer, and no one knows what the future holds (p. 17).
Step 2 (Learn Common Terms in An): Step 2 (Learn 10 Common Terms): They may have been renowned leaders, peacemakers, or lawmakers (p. 17).
Step 3 (Learn Common Terms in An): Step 3 (Learn 10 Common Terms): Some, like Pocahontas, Sacajawea, Hahyonhwatha (known as "Hiawatha"), and Tecumseh, lived centuries ago (p. 17).

Step 4 (Learn Common Terms in An): Step 4 (Learn 10 Common Terms): Others, like Geronimo, Ira Hayes, Ben Night horse Campbell, Ada Deer, and Wilma Mankiller, are people of the 20th and 21st centuries (p. 17).

Step 4 (Life Might Have Been): Step 4 (Describe How Life): See if your town or city has an American Indian center, oran Indian tribal council or similar governing group (p. 9).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why did American Indian nations across regions such as the Pacific Northwest, the Great Plains, and the Desert Southwest develop markedly different housing, diets, and clothing prior to European contact?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why did American Indian nations across regions such as the Pacific Northwest, the Great Plains, and the Desert Southwest develop markedly different housing, diets, and clothing prior to European contact?
options: A. All tribes followed a single continental council that assigned different crafts and housing styles to each region by lottery.
B. Each Indigenous nation adapted its technology, shelter, foodways, and social organization to the specific geography, climate, and natural resources of its homeland.
C. Tribes in every region relied exclusively on imported European iron tools and domesticated horses for thousands of years before 1492.
D. Differences in shelter and diet were caused solely by proximity to Spanish missions established along the Atlantic seaboard.
choices: A. All tribes followed a single continental council that assigned different crafts and housing styles to each region by lottery.
B. Each Indigenous nation adapted its technology, shelter, foodways, and social organization to the specific geography, climate, and natural resources of its homeland.
C. Tribes in every region relied exclusively on imported European iron tools and domesticated horses for thousands of years before 1492.
D. Differences in shelter and diet were caused solely by proximity to Spanish missions established along the Atlantic seaboard.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Each Indigenous nation adapted its technology, shelter, foodways, and social organization to the specific geography, climate, and natural resources of its homeland.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): American Indian cultures developed distinct lifeways (such as cedar plank houses in the Pacific Northwest, bison hide tipis on the Plains, and adobe pueblos in the Southwest) adapted directly to local ecosystems and resources.
